_comment: EVERY Google billing number in this application lives in this file.
No price, free allowance, or quota literal may appear in places/, geo/,
coverage/, search/, or export/ code. Business logic asks the pricing
service instead: classify(fieldMask), remaining(sku), wouldExceed(sku, n).
The values below are UNVERIFIED starting points. Confirm them against the
Google Cloud billing page before the first real run and set verified:true.
Correcting them is a config change, never a code change.
_fieldTiersComment: Maps each field-mask entry to the SKU it forces. Classification is
data-driven so that adding a field cannot silently change the billing
tier: one Enterprise field bills the ENTIRE request at Enterprise.
Phone and website are Enterprise and are both required by the product,
so every lead-search call is an Enterprise call.
VERIFIED against Place Data Fields (New) on 2026-08-21:
https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/places/web-service/data-fields
nextPageToken IS a field-mask-selectable field and DOES carry a SKU. Google
assigns it to 'Text Search Essentials (IDs Only)', the cheapest Text Search
tier, alongside places.id. It must be named in the mask or no page token is
returned at all -- Google's own pagination example is
'X-Goog-FieldMask: places.id,nextPageToken'.
Google bills at the HIGHEST SKU applicable to a request, so an IDs-Only
field participates in classification but can never raise the tier. Mapping
it here at tierRank 1 reproduces that exactly.
Precision note: Google's 'Essentials (IDs Only)' sits one tier BELOW
'Essentials', and this catalog does not model it as a separate SKU. That is
harmless while every lead-search mask carries Enterprise fields, because
rank 1 is already the floor and anything else outranks it. If a future
IDs-only request is ever made, add the SKU then -- do not guess its
allowance now.
Leaving it unmapped is NOT the alternative: an unknown field escalates to
Enterprise by design, which would flag every search as escalated and hide
the one signal meant to warn about a field Google adds later.
